added_claims.speaker: Nick Baltas
added_claims.quote: we're talking about the least correlated environment in the US market in equities which was the consequence of high level of concentration
added_claims.claim: Just before the August 2024 shock US equity correlations were at record lows because returns were concentrated in a few mega-cap AI/tech names; such a low-correlation, high-concentration setup left dispersion and short-correlation trades exposed to a sudden correlation spike.
added_claims.indicator: US equity implied/realized correlation; index concentration
added_claims.direction: correlation up sharply from record lows; dispersion trades lose
added_claims.conditions: high index concentration, crowded dispersion trades
added_claims.testable: yes - implied correlation index levels before shocks

added_claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
added_claims.quote: I don't think it's changed Direction frankly from because the move is relatively short in time only for only for Windows exactly
added_claims.claim: A few-day shock is too short relative to medium/long trend look-back windows to flip equity or yen positions; it mainly causes deleveraging and weaker signal strength while most positions continue, so trend portfolios change little after brief crashes.
added_claims.indicator: trend signal look-back length vs shock duration
added_claims.conditions: short sharp shock followed by rebound
added_claims.testable: yes - simulate signal changes through short shocks

added_claims.speaker: Nick Baltas
added_claims.quote: historically that was the Big Driver of performance and and and over the last like know a year or [L280] two um it has not been
added_claims.claim: Bond futures were historically the main driver of trend-following returns, but after 2022 rates stopped trending and contributed little, which changes how a trend book's returns are composed.
added_claims.indicator: trend P&L attribution by asset class
added_claims.testable: yes - sector attribution of SG Trend / trend replication

added_claims.speaker: Nick Baltas
added_claims.quote: Niki for instance there was substantial intraday momentum that took place on Monday and had you been exposed to those intraday moves
added_claims.claim: On the 5 August 2024 crash day the Nikkei showed strong intraday momentum, so strategies following intraday moves from the open would have profited; the net effect of short-dated option hedging depends on whether dealers are long or short gamma.
added_claims.direction: follow intraday direction from the open
added_claims.conditions: crash days with dealer short gamma
added_claims.testable: yes - intraday momentum returns on high-vol days

added_claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
added_claims.quote: first and foremost we're Risk Managers that's the part of the of the equation we have some input on we have no say in terms of what performance we can get from the markets
added_claims.claim: Trend followers should see themselves first as risk managers because they control risk taken but not returns the market offers; many managers have moved from stop losses with static sizing to VaR-based portfolio risk models, raising the worry that common VaR use synchronizes selling.
added_claims.testable: partly - compare drawdown behaviour of static vs VaR-sized trend books

added_claims.speaker: Nick Baltas
added_claims.quote: if people follow similar rules this cannot in itself have a I guess a contagion effect except the possibility that losses happen at the same time
added_claims.claim: Contagion from risk models comes from many investors suffering losses at the same moment and unwinding together, not from the choice of VaR as such; the real question is whether the measure is right and whether people over- or under-react to it.
added_claims.indicator: VaR / expected shortfall usage across investors
added_claims.testable: partly - flow data around risk-limit breaches

corrections.issue: Wrong year: the caption says 'Thanksgiving 20121', i.e. late November 2021 (the Omicron Black Friday sell-off), not Thanksgiving 2020.
corrections.fix: After the extreme one-day event around Thanksgiving 2021 trend strategies recovered quickly, showing one-day shocks need not damage trend returns.

corrections.issue: Mixes speakers: Niels makes the grain-downtrend point; the observation that non-traditional, non-benchmark commodities gained almost every day in August is Nick Baltas's.
corrections.fix: Niels: strengthening grain downtrends cushioned diversified trend portfolios in July; Nick: alternative non-benchmark commodities added performance almost daily in August 2024, showing the value of diversification insulated from macro moves.

completeness_estimate: 0.87 - first reader was thorough on design choices, speeds and the August 2024 event; missed the pre-shock low-correlation setup, look-back vs shock length, bonds as historical driver, intraday momentum, risk-manager framing and the VaR contagion nuance.
